comparisons.evidence: P's "Personal Technical Rider" and "Grandparenting Stagecraft" reduce recurring setup friction and family-role erosion; Q's "Client Continuity Cooperative" and "Frailty Escrow" target the more consequential bottlenecks of sustained employability and safe transition after diminished capacity.

P clearly links property certification to "fewer failed arrivals" and structured handoffs to overnight expert output; Q similarly links documented backups to lower client key-person risk and portable underwriting to reduced deposits. Both expose their key assumptions through falsifiable tests.

P can begin with a "spreadsheet-based rider," manual overnight reviews, and mailed story kits. Q's strongest portfolio includes a "portable guarantee backed by...pooled underwriting" and a "legally structured control system," which face materially heavier institutional, regulatory, and cross-jurisdictional dependencies.

P specifies a rider with "15–25 variables," an arrival test, users, payers, and pilot measurements; Q specifies documented work, nominated backups, contractual guarantees, and concrete adoption tests. Both make the proposed change and first prototype readily understandable.

P offers unusually fresh causal levers such as commitments that "decay by default" and distance becoming a physical storytelling mechanic in "Grandparenting Stagecraft." Q's "being needed" Role Guild and pooled continuity are thoughtful reframings, but more closely resemble service clubs, cooperatives, guarantees, and advance directives.

P credibly spans environmental standardization, asynchronous expert work, family play, and automatic commitment expiry. Q reaches further across distinct institutional pathways: professional risk pooling, housing underwriting, delegated authority, reciprocal roles, task custody, fraud attestation, settlement options, and multi-party home exchange.

P retains several adjacent continuity-diagnostics mechanisms, including "Handoff Ledger," "Continuity Maintenance Schedule," "Delegation Ladder," "Location Dependency Graph," and "Load-Shed Switch." Q more consistently separates pathways, explicitly distinguishing, for example, "Frailty Escrow" as decision governance from "One-Click Landing" as reserved physical capacity.
